title: The Market’s Fed Watch in Action | Dimensional
gist: Dimensional's Wes Crill uses the Fed's September 2026 25 bp hike to show that markets priced it before it happened. Fed-funds futures went from a near-zero hike probability on May 1 to more than 90% after a hot CPI print. The one-year Treasury yield rose about 22 bps around the CPI release, roughly the size of the hike, then barely moved on the announcement itself.

insights.claim: The US Federal Reserve raised the federal-funds rate by 25 basis points at its September 2026 meeting, a move that fed-funds futures had priced at near-zero probability as recently as May 1, 2026.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: Rate expectations in 2026 are volatile: a policy path that was priced out four months earlier happened anyway, so do not anchor duration positioning to distant futures pricing.
insights.quote: As recently as May 1, fed-funds futures pricing implied a near-zero probability of rates going up at the September meeting.

insights.claim: An unexpectedly high CPI print ahead of the Fed's September 2026 meeting pushed the market-implied probability of a rate hike, as measured by the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, to more than 90%.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: Inflation surprises are driving the Fed's reaction function in 2026; CPI releases are the key repricing events for front-end rates.
insights.quote: an unexpectedly high September consumer price index (CPI) print was followed by the rate hike probability cresting 90%

insights.claim: The one-year US Treasury yield rose about 22 bps in the days around the hot CPI release, roughly the same as the 25 bp Fed hike that followed. It then held flat until the announcement, so the hike itself caused little reaction in bond yields.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: The front-end move happens on the data surprise, not on the meeting day, so positioning trades for a hike after the CPI print is out capture little.
insights.quote: the one-year US Treasury yield jumped by about 22 bps in the days surrounding the CPI release—roughly equivalent to the magnitude of the eventual hike
insights.locator: Exhibit 1: One-Year US Treasury Yield, September 1–16, 2026

insights.claim: After the September 2026 hike was announced, the one-year Treasury yield rose only slightly, and that move was attributed to Fed signals of a possible further rate increase later in 2026 rather than to the hike itself.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: On announcement day, yields respond to guidance about future moves rather than the decision itself. Watch Fed forward guidance on another 2026 hike as the next driver of front-end yields.
insights.quote: rising again slightly amid signals of another possible increase this year

themes.theme: Market efficiency argument against timing Fed moves

insights.claim: Bond markets are forward-looking and price Fed rate decisions into Treasury yields before they happen, so investors who expect a large yield reaction to a Fed announcement will often be surprised.
insights.speaker: Wes Crill
insights.so_what: Dimensional's efficient-markets view: trading bonds on a Fed decision everyone expects adds little. Any edge has to come from predicting data surprises better than the market does.
insights.quote: This demonstrates the forward-looking nature of markets, pricing in the Fed’s actions before they take place.

source_meta.author: Wes Crill, PhD, Senior Client Solutions Director and Vice President
